newsitem.title: USA: Int'l Rectifier sees lower Q1 earnings.
newsitem.headline: Int'l Rectifier sees lower Q1 earnings.

text.p: International Rectifier Corp said Thursday first quarter earnings will fall below expectations because aggressive efforts by distributors to reduce inventories has hurt orders and shipments.

The company said it expects first quarter net profits of between $0.05 and $0.10 a share on revenues of $115 to $125 million compared with a profit of $0.25 a share on revenues of $126 million in the year-ago quarter.
Analysts had forecasted the company would post earnings per share of $0.28 for the first quarter, according to First Call.
International Rectifier said its long term outlook remains positive.

The company also said competitive price moves in August resulted in 10 to 15 percent average lower prices on about one-third of IR's business, and that order cancellations are cutting deeply into its backlog.

The company said that end-use demand remains stable in the quarter and that the inventory correction should be largely completed by the end of December. IR said it expects competitive pressure to result in lower prices on about half its business.
Non-critical hiring and expenditures are being deferred until the company sees a decisive improvement in business conditions.
